turns.user: what does section 123B of the PPC actually make an offence, and how much jail time can someone get under it?

gold.answer: Section 123B of the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860 punishes deliberately defiling or setting fire to the National Flag of Pakistan, or removing it without authority from any Government building, premises, vehicle or other property. The punishment is imprisonment of either description up to three years, or fine, or both.

evidence.quote: Whoever deliberately defiles [or puts on fire] the National Flag of Pakistan, or unauthorisedly removes it from any building, premises, vehicle or other property of Government, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with fine, or with both.

turns.user: If I'm the one being indemnified and I get sued, what exactly can I claim back from the other person under section 125 of the Contract Act, 1872?

gold.answer: Under section 125 of the Contract Act, 1872 the promisee (indemnity-holder) can recover from the promisor all damages he is compelled to pay in the suit, all costs of the suit, and any sums paid under a prudent compromise of the suit, subject to the conditions in the section.

evidence.quote: The promisee in a contract of indemnity, acting within the scope of his authority, is entitled to recover from the promisor___ (1) all damages which he may be compelled to pay in any suit

evidence.quote: Article 159 of the 1st Schedule to the Limitation Act, 1908 prescribes a period of ten days for filing of leave to appeal and defend a suit in summary proceedings and the said time is to run from when the summons are served.
